# JobsLocked — full site text

JobsLocked is an AI receptionist, booking and review service for US contractors and home-service businesses. A product of Antek Automation — UK-founded, serving US contractors. Contact: hello@jobslocked.com. Tagline: "Jobs locked in. While you're on the tools."

---

## Home — https://jobslocked.com/

# The call you missed was the job you needed.

You're on a roof, in a crawlspace, under a sink. Your phone rings. It goes to voicemail. They don't leave one — they call the next name on the list. JobsLocked answers that call, holds the conversation, and books the job into your calendar before you've climbed down.

Homeowners with a problem call three contractors. The first one to answer gets the job.

## It's not a marketing problem. It's a phone problem.

You don't need more calls. You need to stop losing the ones you already paid for.

- **They don't leave voicemails.** Around 8 in 10 callers who hit voicemail hang up and dial the next number. A homeowner with a problem isn't waiting for a callback.
- **Your callback is too late.** By the time you're off the ladder, they've had a quote from someone who picked up. You're now the second opinion, if you're anything.
- **Every missed call is your ad money, burned.** Google, Angi, Yelp, the truck wrap — you paid for that ring. Voicemail throws the receipt away.

## What happens now when your phone rings

1. **It answers.** Second ring, every time. Your business name, a calm voice, and the first question: "What's going on at the house?"
2. **It holds the conversation.** Address, what's wrong, how long it's been going on, urgent or can it wait. The questions you'd ask — without you asking them.
3. **It books the job.** Reads your live calendar, offers real slots, locks one in. Confirmation text to them. Summary text to you.
4. **It follows up.** Hung up early? Text-back inside a minute. Sent a form at 11 PM? Callback inside 60 seconds. Texted or WhatsApped? Answered.

## Every plan starts here. No exceptions.

Whatever door a customer comes through, they get an answer in under 60 seconds — day, night, weekend. And every finished job gets asked for the review.

- AI receptionist answers every call, 24/7
- Books the job straight into your calendar
- Missed-call text-back if a caller hangs up early
- Replies to SMS and WhatsApp enquiries instantly
- Calls back web-form leads within 60 seconds
- Texts you a summary of every conversation
- Hands real emergencies to you live
- Review request texted after every finished job — direct Google link

## Three plans. One receptionist. It just goes further.

Every plan answers every call, books the job and asks for the review. The higher plans keep working after the first conversation.

## What it won't do

It won't pretend to be you. It won't quote a price you didn't give it. It won't promise a time your calendar doesn't have. And it won't replace the people you've already got — it catches what they can't, when they can't.

## Straight answers (FAQ)

**Will customers know it's not a person?** If they ask, it tells them. Most don't ask — they've got a problem in the house and they want someone booked. It sounds calm, gets the address, the problem, and a time, and stops there.

**What happens on a real emergency?** It asks two questions, then rings you live. If you don't pick up, it books the earliest slot and tells the caller exactly when you'll be there.

**Does it quote prices?** Only the ranges you give it, and only if you want it to. Default is "the owner will confirm on site." It never invents a number.

**Can I keep my number?** Yes. We forward your existing number, or give you a new tracking number for ads. Either way your customers dial what they've always dialed.

**How long until it's live?** Setup call, then about a week to build and test with your real job types. You hear it before a customer does.

**Am I locked into a contract?** Month to month. The setup fee covers the build; the plan covers the running. Leave whenever it stops paying for itself.

## Stop losing the calls you already paid for.

Fifteen minutes. You describe a typical job, we show you the receptionist taking that exact call. Book at https://jobslocked.com/book/ — slots mornings and lunchtimes, Eastern.

- 3:10 PM — Morning job marked done. Customer gets a text with a direct link to your Google review page. Five stars by 3:40.

## Plan 2: Book Every Job — https://jobslocked.com/plans/book-every-job/

$649/mo · 600 minutes included · Setup about a week. Most chosen plan.

Answering the call is where most contractors lose. Following up is where the rest do. This plan keeps the receptionist working after the first conversation — chasing the ones who didn't book, handling the customers you already have, and showing you every enquiry in one place.

**Who this is for:** You've got a website, some ad spend, and a phone that's already busy. Enquiries come in from four directions and some fall through the gaps — the form that got a reply but not a booking, the customer who wanted to reschedule and never got an answer, the quote that went quiet. You want one receptionist across all of it.

**A Tuesday with it running:**
- 8:15 AM — Website chat opens. Same receptionist, same questions, booked for Thursday. No form, no waiting.
- 9:40 AM — Existing customer calls about the invoice from last week. Answered, sorted, no interruption to your morning.
- 11:00 AM — Monday's caller who said 'let me think about it' gets a text: 'Still want that looked at? We've got Wednesday open.' Booked.
- 3:30 PM — You open the pipeline. Nine enquiries this week, six booked, two chasing, one closed-lost. You know exactly where the money is.

**What you get:**
- Everything in Never Miss a Call
- Website chat answered by the same receptionist
- Follow-up sequences: unbooked enquiries chased for days, by text, until they book or say no
- Existing-customer handling: job status, reschedules, invoice questions
- Every enquiry — call, text, chat, form — tracked in a pipeline you can open on your phone
- 600 receptionist minutes a month included
- Month to month, one-time setup fee
